PDS Wave 20 — Derive the Real Floor, Then Fire

Wave strategy Paper. Opened at Strategize (surveying). The living story of the wave — every later phase appends here. Root task: pds-w1-crown-proof. Prior wave: pds-wave-19-2026-07-21.

The wish

THIS CYCLE: PDS WAVE 20 — DERIVE THE REAL FLOOR, THEN FIRE. The crown climb is armed and healthy but CANNOT fire: in 618 draws over ~1h45m, guerrilla MemAvailable ranged 1796–2012 MiB and cleared the 2200 floor ZERO times. The 2200 floor is a FOSSIL from the retired in-RAM engine; the deployed streaming spill engine's real peak is ~477 MiB. This wave DERIVES a correct floor against the deployed engine (doctrine-compliant, env-only), arms at that floor, and fires in the box's actual memory regime.

Where the epic stands

The crown proof (pds-w1-crown-proof) reads 9 of 12. Criteria 0–5, 7–9 are met from the wave-7 climb; 6, 10, 11 are unmet:

• 6 — content-and-presence convergence across a real reboot (PDS-D75), needs the fire's own pull.
• 10 — PR merged to main, LEAD-closed on merge (merge-gated, PDS-D163).
• 11 — the single-run attribution fence (PDS-D234): every one of 0–10 must cite ONE identical RUN_ID, and that run's full bundle must actually have existed. No mosaic.

The crown is one green run away — but that run must re-take rungs 3+4 (the full export, feeding criteria 8/9) AND green rung 6, all under one RUN_ID. Waves 13–19 each tried and none fired.

The pattern of failure, precisely:

• Wave 13 — died to agent-turn length: the poller was cut at poll 3 of 30 and reclaimed with the worktree. The fix was detach the fire from the agent turn (pds-crown-launch.sh — python os.fork()+os.setsid()+os.execvp; nohup/setsid(1) don't survive here, PDS-D243).
• Waves 14–19 — the detached architecture worked; the box did not cooperate. Wave 19 armed a clean detached climb and measured, at L1 over 618 draws / ~1h45m (run c7528814): MemAvailable min 1796 / max 2012, draws clearing the 2200 floor = 0 of 618. The box's live regime does not reach 2200. It is not a volatile window — it is a wall the box never crosses.

The decisive finding: 2200 is a fossil, and a hardcoded law enforces it

PDS_FULL_EXPORT_MIN_MEM_MB default 2200 is the RETIRED in-RAM engine's number — that engine materialised the whole ~941 MB tar as one BEAM binary and peaked at a measured ~2235 MiB incremental demand (PDS-D185/D222). That engine is gone. The DEPLOYED engine is the streaming spill engine (#5083): it streams COPY in 500-row chunks and spills to disk, so its RAM peak is bounded by chunk size, not bundle size. Three independent readings agree it is a few hundred MiB, not 2235:

• PDS-D217 — worst 500-row COPY chunk = 19.71 MiB wire bytes (mutation_events), 0.9% of 2200.
• Wave 16 empirical fire — a real ~1.4 GB full export fired at MemAvailable 2578, prod stayed HEALTHY (GET /api/schemas 200 in 0.14 s, MemAvailable 1931 after), zero dmesg OOM lines.
• The ride-along observation (PDS-D253) — the parked bundle's own 1 Hz sampler put the incremental RSS peak at ~477 MiB — but PDS-D253 ruled this an UNRATIFIED observation, deliberately declining to name it the PDS-D211/D222 demand figure, because no real unscoped export had yet been ridden (open task pds-bl-ratify-or-discard-ridealong-demand).

And a hard guard enforces the fossil. scripts/pds-crown-launch.sh:125 hardcodes MEM_FLOOR_LAW=2200 (a bare literal, no env override), and cmd_arm (:412-413) refuses to arm when the poll floor PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB is below it: "the predicate tightens only." PDS-D244 additionally leaves the harness floor PDS_FULL_EXPORT_MIN_MEM_MB UNSET so 2200 stands. So the fire literally cannot happen below 2200 today — this is not "arm and fire." The wave must move the law itself, by derivation, exactly as PDS-D211 permits and requires.

Direction

Derive the real floor against the deployed spill engine, lower BOTH floor knobs to it by that derivation, fire the detached climb in the box's actual regime, and let the climb's own export ratify the floor post-hoc. The finished experience: the crown climb finally fires — takes its own fresh full export at a derived floor of roughly ~1276 MiB (well under the 1796 regime floor, far above any plausible peak), the ride-along sampler measures the authoritative peak, that peak ratifies the derived floor (converting PDS-D253's unratified observation into the licensed demand figure and closing pds-bl-ratify-or-discard-ridealong-demand), all 12 criteria green under ONE RUN_ID, and the crown seals 12/12. The honest alternative — a NAMED refusal (e.g. sampler peak exceeds floor−margin → re-derive upward, filed) — is still a win. Wave-16's evidence makes GREEN the expected outcome.

Three moves, in sequence:

1. DERIVE the floor. FLOOR = measured_demand_delta + margin (PDS-D222: a delta, never the absolute peak; margin 798.81 MiB, the max observed drawdown). The demand delta is the streaming engine's real RSS peak-minus-baseline, grounded in the wave-16 healthy fire and the ~477 ride-along observation — NOT the 19.71 wire-byte figure (mixing wire bytes into an RSS floor is the PDS-D185 unit error that made PDS-D232 refuse). Roughly 477 + 799 ≈ 1276 MiB, subject to the survey nailing the demand number's provenance. Commit the derivation record; supersede PDS-D232/D244 in the charter.
2. ARM the floor into both instruments — a surgical pds-crown-launch.sh edit (within the scripts/pds-* fence): lower MEM_FLOOR_LAW from the fossil 2200 to the derived value so the launcher's poll predicate will fire in-regime, and set PDS_FULL_EXPORT_MIN_MEM_MB to the derived value in cmd_arm's contiguous env-export block so the harness child's gate (b) matches (reversing D244). Both floors move by the same derived number; the anti-loosening guard is preserved, now guarding the DERIVED law instead of the fossil. Record the floor in run_dir/meta and the summary (closing pds-bl-w16-arm-never-records-its-own-floor). The frozen harness blob (e219e97ccf7f33797c86a2b84d998d599b6bda31, pds-pull-proof.sh) is untouched — the harness only READS the env we now export.
3. FIRE + collect. Arm the detached climb at the live c7528814 scratch (BARKPARK_HOME /private/tmp/pds-w14.c7528814, reuse handle PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw18-crown), ride the stripped D237 sampler alongside (zero export cost, MUST NOT gate/delay the fire), embed $RUN_TAG (D233), --all, one run, archive/override PDS_LAUNCH_STATE_DIR to dodge the single-run mosaic (criterion 11). Arm detached, return, DO NOT poll. The LEAD collects: ratifies the ride-along peak, stamps criterion 6, closes 10 on merge, stamps 11 alone LAST after verifying all eleven ids are identical.

Leans (Decide finalises after two explore rounds): builders fable by default (Fable 5 spend is back); reserve opus for the derivation+launcher-edit slice (subtle correctness — unit discipline, two-knob consistency, doctrine reversal). Zero new scripts; every instrument is merged — only the launcher's floor knobs move, plus the derivation record, charter, transcript, and fire record.

Direction debate

Rival A (WINNER) — Derive from existing evidence, arm at the derived floor, self-ratify by firing. Break the deadlock by not requiring a fresh out-of-band measurement before firing: derive a conservative-but-correct floor from wave-16's healthy fire + the ride-along observation + D222's margin, arm, fire, and let the climb's OWN full export produce the authoritative ratifying peak. The floor sits ~800 MiB above demand and ~500 MiB below the regime, so it fires in-regime and stays provably safe.

Rival B — Measure out-of-band FIRST (the wave-12 chain), then arm. Run pds-export-peak-measure.sh for a fresh D104-controlled peak-minus-baseline, apply D222, set the floor, then arm. Loses: structurally blocked, and it is the trap that has cost the epic multiple waves. The scoped export refuses itself (non_positive_delta, delta below BEAM oscillation, wave 14); the only measurement that yields a floor is an unscoped ~1.4 GB full export, which itself needs the floor already lowered to run (the PDS-D219 bootstrap deadlock) AND needs MemAvailable above the measure gate (the box doesn't have it) AND D221 voids the idle control in this regime (live range ~1664 MiB > the 1048.16 MiB void threshold). It also spends a full export out-of-band, then the climb spends another — double the memory cost, and the out-of-band one buys nothing the climb's own ride-along doesn't. pds-bl-floor-derivation-needs-a-real-acquisition is the filed proof that no zero-cost route exists — so the cheapest real acquisition is the climb itself.

Rival C — Don't derive; raise the budget and fire at 2200, wait for a window (wave-13's D232). Loses: wave 19 PROVED 0/618 draws cross 2200 over ~1h45m. The window does not exist in this regime. Firing at 2200 = never firing. This is the fossil wall, and four waves have already broken on it.

Rival D — Fix the engine / add server-side serialization / a cgroup cap so the floor can be even lower. Loses: scope creep across the fence (engine/api are OFF this wave — scripts/pds-* ONLY), and PDS-D218 already PROVED the watchdog/cgroup cap is unbuildable here (MemoryMax=infinity, OOMPolicy=stop). The engine is already fine — streaming spill, peak in the hundreds of MiB. The problem is purely the floor VALUE, which is env-plus-one-literal.

Why A wins: the epic has been stuck for waves oscillating between B (measure-first, blocked) and C (fire-at-2200, never fires). A is the only path that both (i) respects the PDS-D211 derivation law and (ii) fires in the regime the box actually has — because it derives from evidence already in hand and makes the fire produce its own ratifying measurement, sidestepping the bootstrap deadlock entirely.

Sharpest attack on A: The ~477 demand number is not a clean, doctrine-compliant delta. If it is a wire-byte figure or an uncontrolled RSS sample, then FLOOR = 477 + 799 rests on a number PDS-D185/ D232 would reject — and worse, if 477 understates the true streaming-engine peak, the derived floor could sit BELOW real demand (violating PDS-D211), so the climb fires into a floor that doesn't protect the box, and a build-storm mid-export OOMs the live content API (OOMPolicy=stop kills the API, not the export).

How the wave absorbs it:

• The survey PROVES the ~477 provenance (wave-16 paper + the ride-along record). If it is an RSS peak-minus-baseline from a real streaming-engine full export, it is unit-clean and D185 does not bite. If it is not fully clean, the derivation uses the best available real RSS delta and states the honesty limit — the floor's safety rests on floor ≫ peak, not on a perfect control.
• The D222 margin (798.81 MiB) is the measured max drawdown — a generous, box-volatility figure. Even if 477 understates true demand by hundreds of MiB, the ~1276 floor still sits far above it.
• Ratification is built in. The floor is provisional-until-the-fire: the stripped sampler measures the authoritative peak during the real export, and if that peak exceeds floor − margin it is a NAMED failure — filed, floor re-derived upward, the shot re-armed (a closed/failed gate costs zero export attempts). The fire produces its own proof.
• The streaming engine spills to disk; its RAM peak is chunk-bounded (~20 MiB wire / ~477 MiB RSS), and the box showed zero dmesg OOM lines under a build storm at 1571 MiB worst against this consumer (PDS-D218/D230). The 2235 demand belonged to an engine that no longer runs.
